value.note: je place, ils placent, vous placez; no cedilla before e/i.
-cer verb: cedilla before o to keep /s/ (source attests nous plaçons).
je plaçais; the participle plaçant shows the same change (attested).
je placerai; also conditional je placerais.
que nous placions; the singular subjunctive shares the plac- stem of the present.

evidence.notes: Regular 1st-group -cer verb; source attests nous plaçons, confirming the c/ç alternation.

value.note: je plagie, ils plagient (to plagiarize).
nous plagions, vous plagiez.
je plagiais.
je plagierai; also conditional je plagierais.
que nous plagiions (double i before the ending).

evidence.notes: Regular 1st-group -ier verb; the stem keeps its i throughout, with ii in the nous/vous imperfect and subjunctive forms.

value.note: -aindre verb: je plains, tu plains, il plaint.
d becomes gn before a vowel: nous plaignons, vous plaignez, ils plaignent.
je plaignais.
je plaindrai; conditional je plaindrais.
que je plaigne (se plaindre de = to complain about).
Past participle plaint; the passé simple stem is plaign- (je plaignis).

evidence.notes: Irregular 3rd-group -aindre verb; related_context names plaindre as a member of the peindre group, so the plain-/plaign-/plaindr-/plaint- stems follow that model.

value.note: Short stem: je plais, tu plais, il plaît (attested, circumflex on the il form).
nous plaisons, vous plaisez, ils plaisent (attested).
je plaisais.
je plairai; conditional je plairais.
que je plaise.
Irregular past participle plu (attested); the attested passé simple il plut / ils plurent uses the same stem.

evidence.notes: Irregular 3rd-group -aire verb taking à; the present paradigm, participle plu and passé simple forms are attested in related_context.

value.note: je plaisante, ils plaisantent (to joke).
nous plaisantons, vous plaisantez.
je plaisantais.
je plaisanterai.
que je plaisante.

evidence.notes: Fully regular 1st-group -er verb; no stem alternation beyond the regular future stem.
